name: War
description: War is a simple children's card game. 2 players. 52-card deck split evenly. Both flip top card simultaneously — higher wins both. Tie = 'War': each plays 1 face-down then 1 face-up; higher face-up wins all. Continue until one player has all cards. Pure luck — no decisions.

content.text: War is a simple children's card game. 2 players. 52-card deck split evenly. Both flip top card simultaneously — higher wins both. Tie = 'War': each plays 1 face-down then 1 face-up; higher face-up wins all. Continue until one player has all cards. Pure luck — no decisions.

War is a children's comparison card game played in many parts of the world. No single inventor or date is documented; it has long been passed on as a first card game. In the United Kingdom it is often called Battle. Related regional forms include the Russian P'yanitsa (Drunkard), the German Tod und Leben (Life and Death), and Syrian War, indicating broad dissemination across Europe and beyond. The core mechanic—simultaneously revealing cards and the higher rank capturing both—is one of the simplest card-game structures and requires no strategy, only the ability to compare ranks.
52 cards. A high. Split deck evenly 26-26.

items.text: Three face-down war: In a war, each player plays three cards face down then one face up (ten cards total). Whoever has the higher face-up card wins all ten. If a player has fewer than four cards, some play that the player with fewest cards uses all their cards and the other plays the same number.

War with two jokers: Two jokers are added to the pack and count as the highest cards, above aces. To avoid one player getting both, some separate the jokers before dividing the deck and bury one joker in each player's stack.
